properties.name: stx.errors.enabled
properties.description: Register the stx error handling. Off unless set: putting this library on the classpath must not change how an application already reports failures.

properties.name: stx.errors.include-debug-message
properties.description: Serialize ApiException.debugMessage into the response. Leave off outside development: a debug message is routinely a query, a constraint name or an upstream body.

properties.name: stx.security.enabled
properties.description: Register the stx security beans: a BCrypt PasswordEncoder and the meta-annotation template support that @RequireRole needs. Not a filter chain — which paths are open stays the application's decision.

properties.name: stx.security.bcrypt-strength
properties.description: The BCrypt work factor. Each step doubles the cost to hash and to attack. Raising it does not invalidate existing hashes: the cost is stored in the hash.

properties.name: stx.cors.enabled
properties.description: Register the CORS filter built from these properties.

properties.name: stx.cors.origins
properties.description: The exact origins allowed. Empty by default: a browser policy that arrives already permitting somebody is the wrong shape of default.

properties.name: stx.cors.origin-patterns
properties.description: Origins matched as patterns, so one entry covers every subdomain. The one that works with allow-credentials, because the concrete requesting origin is echoed back rather than a wildcard.

properties.name: stx.cors.methods
properties.description: The HTTP methods those origins may use.

properties.name: stx.cors.headers
properties.description: The request headers those origins may send.

properties.name: stx.cors.exposed-headers
properties.description: The response headers the browser is allowed to read. Empty means the CORS-safelisted ones.

properties.name: stx.cors.allow-credentials
properties.description: Whether the browser may send cookies and Authorization. Cannot be combined with an origins list of "*" — use origin-patterns.

properties.name: stx.cors.max-age
properties.description: How long a browser may cache the preflight answer, in seconds.

properties.name: stx.cors.path
properties.description: The path pattern this CORS configuration applies to.

properties.name: stx.json.enabled
properties.description: Make kotlinx-serialization the codec WebFlux reads and writes JSON with, in place of Jackson. Off because kotlinx serializes only what carries @Serializable, and switching a running application over is a decision rather than a detail.

properties.name: stx.json.explicit-nulls
properties.description: Whether a null property is written out at all. Off, so a response type with a dozen optional fields is not mostly nulls.

properties.name: stx.json.encode-defaults
properties.description: Whether a property equal to its default is written out. On, the opposite of the kotlinx default: a client that has never seen a field cannot know the default the server would have used.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.enabled
properties.description: Register the stx Spring Data Mongo beans, starting with the kotlin.time.Instant converters. Separate from stx.mongo, which is the stx-mongo driver library's own integration.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.gridfs-bucket
properties.description: The GridFS bucket a ReactiveGridFsTemplate is opened on. Unset means no template: a bucket that appears because nobody set a property is two collections in a database that never asked for them.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.transactions
properties.description: Register a ReactiveMongoTransactionManager. Needs a replica set — a standalone mongod fails the first startTransaction rather than at startup.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.auditor
properties.description: Register a ReactiveAuditorAware answering with the authenticated user's name, so @CreatedBy and @LastModifiedBy fill themselves in. Distinct from stx.data.mongo.audit, which keeps the document's whole history. Needs Spring Security, and @EnableReactiveMongoAuditing in the application.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.create-indexes
properties.description: Create the indexes the mapped entities declare, once the application is ready. Nothing is ever dropped: rebuilding an index on a live collection means every query using it scans until it is done.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.audit.enabled
properties.description: Record every save and delete of an @Auditable document as a version in a collection of its own. Off by default: an audit trail is a second copy of the data and a deployment's decision.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.audit.collection
properties.description: The collection audit entries are written to. Changing it after entries exist starts a new, empty history.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.migration.enabled
properties.description: Run pending migrations after the application is ready. Off by default: the version this was extracted from defaulted to true, which meant putting the library on a classpath was enough to have it write to the database.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.migration.prefix
properties.description: What a migration class name starts with, before its order — V gives V3Currencies. Matched literally, so a prefix containing a . is a . and not a wildcard.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.migration.collection
properties.description: The collection migration records are written to. It is what makes a migration run once, so pointing it at an empty collection runs every migration again.

properties.name: stx.mongo.enabled
properties.description: Open an stx-mongo coroutine client. Off by default. Distinct from stx.data.mongo and from Spring Boot's spring.data.mongodb, which configure Spring Data's ReactiveMongoTemplate — a different API onto the same server, and a second pool if both are on.

properties.name: stx.mongo.uri
properties.description: The connection string. Required when enabled: a default would be a guess about somebody's cluster.

properties.name: stx.mongo.database
properties.description: The database the MongoDatabase bean points at. Required when enabled.

properties.name: stx.jpa.enabled
properties.description: Build a Hibernate Reactive session factory at startup. Off by default.

properties.name: stx.jpa.uri
properties.description: postgresql://host:port/database, the way a reactive driver spells it. Not a JDBC URL — a jdbc: prefix is the first thing to suspect when a connection fails for no visible reason.

properties.name: stx.jpa.username
properties.description: Sent separately, because the URI does not carry it and must not be made to.

properties.name: stx.jpa.password
properties.description: Sent separately, for the same reason.

properties.name: stx.jpa.schema
properties.description: The default schema for unqualified table names. Left to the server's search_path when unset.

properties.name: stx.jpa.packages
properties.description: The packages entities are scanned from. Required when enabled. The scan also finds @Converters, which naming classes one by one does not.

properties.name: stx.jpa.naming
properties.description: What a column is called when the entity does not say. created_by, not createdby.

properties.name: stx.jpa.schema-mode
properties.description: What Hibernate does to the schema at startup. none outside tests: a schema is migrated by something that keeps a history, not by an ORM inferring one from the classes it was handed.

properties.name: stx.jpa.pool-size
properties.description: How many connections the pool holds. A reactive pool is not sized like a blocking one — a connection is held for the length of a statement, not of a request.

properties.name: stx.jpa.connect-timeout
properties.description: How long to wait for a connection before failing. A java.time.Duration (30s, PT30S): the binder has never heard of kotlin.time.Duration.

properties.name: stx.jpa.idle-timeout
properties.description: How long an idle connection is kept before the pool closes it.

properties.name: stx.jpa.statement-cache-size
properties.description: How many prepared statements each connection caches. Off in the driver by default.

properties.name: stx.jpa.batch-size
properties.description: How many inserts or updates Hibernate sends in one batch. Unset is one statement per row.

properties.name: stx.jpa.show-sql
properties.description: Log every statement. Useful once, expensive always.

properties.name: stx.jpa.properties
properties.description: Anything else Hibernate understands, applied last and overriding everything above.

properties.name: stx.storage.enabled
properties.description: Open an stx-storage connection. Off by default.

properties.name: stx.storage.endpoint
properties.description: Where the store is. MinIO, S3, or anything speaking S3. Required when enabled.

properties.name: stx.storage.access-key
properties.description: Required when enabled, and with no default on purpose: a credential with a default is a credential in source control.

properties.name: stx.storage.secret-key
properties.description: Required when enabled, and with no default, for the same reason.

properties.name: stx.storage.region
properties.description: Can stay unset against MinIO. Against S3 itself it usually cannot: the SDK will otherwise ask the service where a bucket lives, once per bucket the first time it sees one.

properties.name: stx.redis.enabled
properties.description: Open an stx-redis connection. Off by default. Not spring.data.redis, which configures Spring Data's own template over a different client.

properties.name: stx.redis.uri
properties.description: Where the server is.

properties.name: stx.redis.namespace
properties.description: Prefixed to every key this application writes. Worth setting whenever the server is shared: Redis has one flat keyspace per database, so two applications with a session: key and no namespace are one application overwriting the other.

properties.name: stx.redis.timeout
properties.description: How long a command waits before failing. A java.time.Duration (10s, PT10S): the binder has never heard of kotlin.time.Duration.

properties.name: stx.kafka.enabled
properties.description: Register the stx-kafka cluster handle. Off by default. It opens nothing: the connections belong to the publishers and subscribers it hands out.

properties.name: stx.kafka.bootstrap
properties.description: host:port pairs, comma-separated.

properties.name: stx.kafka.client-id
properties.description: What this application calls itself to the broker. Worth setting: it is what the broker's metrics and logs name, and consumer-1 in an incident is not a name.

properties.name: stx.kafka.properties
properties.description: Anything else the clients understand, applied last.

properties.name: stx.amqp.enabled
properties.description: Open an stx-amqp connection at startup. Off by default. Unlike stx.jpa this really does open a socket at startup, so a broker that is not there fails the boot rather than the first publish.

properties.name: stx.amqp.uri
properties.description: Host, port, virtual host and credentials. The default vhost is named / while a URI path of / means the empty vhost, so amqp://localhost:5672/ authenticates against a vhost most brokers do not have and fails about permissions rather than about spelling. Write amqp://localhost:5672 or amqp://localhost:5672/%2F.

properties.name: stx.amqp.connection-name
properties.description: What this connection calls itself in the broker's management UI. Worth setting.

properties.name: stx.amqp.heartbeat
properties.description: What makes a dead connection look dead. Without it a broker restart or a dropped NAT mapping leaves a socket that reads as open and delivers nothing.

properties.name: stx.amqp.connection-timeout
properties.description: How long to wait for the connection itself.

properties.name: stx.amqp.recovery
properties.description: Reconnect and re-declare after a broker restart.

properties.name: stx.i18n.enabled
properties.description: Load the message catalogs and narrow the locale resolver to the languages named below. Off by default.

properties.name: stx.i18n.languages
properties.description: The languages with catalogs — [en, fr], or [en, fr-CA] for a region. The version this replaces hardcoded en and fr in a @Configuration class.

properties.name: stx.i18n.fallback
properties.description: The language a key falls back to when the request's has no text for it. Per key, not per request.

properties.name: stx.i18n.base-name
properties.description: Where the .properties catalogs are — locales/messages_fr.properties for fr.

properties.name: stx.i18n.fail-on-missing-key
properties.description: Throw on a key with no text anywhere, instead of returning the key. Off in a deployment and worth turning on in a test suite: a running server should not fail a request over a translation, and a test suite should not pass over one.
